attributes.description: AWS region everything is created in.
Repository name, used as the prefix of every resource.
Environment name: staging or production.
Tag of the image the function runs. CI rewrites it on every deploy; `bootstrap` before the first one.
Retriever the chain talks to: qdrant (deployed) or local (development only, the image ships no index).
Qdrant Cloud cluster URL (https://<id>.<region>.aws.cloud.qdrant.io). Its API key goes in the SecureString, not here.
Ollama HTTP API the chain calls. Must be reachable from Lambda: the localhost default only works for a local run.
Model the chain generates with.
Embedding model served by the same Ollama API, used at index time and at query time.
Function memory. CPU scales with it, so this is the knob for latency: 1024 MB keeps a retrieval round trip to a couple of seconds.
Function timeout. The chain waits on Ollama, so it is generous compared with a CPU-bound handler.
Hard ceiling on concurrent invocations, and the only guard that actually caps what a reachable URL can spend. -1 leaves the account-wide pool unbounded.
AWS_IAM keeps the endpoint private (callers sign with SigV4); NONE makes it public, so anyone with the URL can spend model time on the Ollama host.
Budget alarm threshold. The stack idles under a dollar, so this alarm is meant to fire when something is actually wrong.
Address the budget alarm and the CloudWatch alarms write to.
owner/name of the repository allowed to deploy.
Branch whose pushes may assume the deploy role.
Thumbprint of the token.actions.githubusercontent.com certificate. Only used when this configuration creates the provider.
Set to false when the account already has the token.actions.githubusercontent.com provider: AWS allows only one per account and apply fails with EntityAlreadyExists.
JSON body of the application secret. Placeholders by default: replace the value with `aws ssm put-parameter --overwrite` after apply, so the real credentials never sit in a .tfvars file.
